firmographic.name: Cal.com
firmographic.company_description:
Cal.com, founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco (operating as a fully distributed team), sells scheduling infrastructure SaaS to individuals, teams, organizations, and regulated enterprises. The product eliminates meeting back-and-forth through shareable booking links, native calendar synchronization across Google Calendar, Outlook, and 100+ providers via the Unified Calendar API, automated SMS/email reminders via Twilio, embedded scheduling widgets (Cal Atoms and Cal.com Embed), and built-in video conferencing (Cal Video, powered by Daily.co). Compliance posture spans SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA, supporting healthcare and other regulated buyers; the platform supports 65+ languages and is offered both as a multi-tenant SaaS at app.cal.com and historically as a self-hostable deployment via GitHub.

The company monetizes through a freemium model: a free individual tier, a $16/user/month Teams tier, a $37/user/month Organizations tier, and custom-priced Enterprise contracts with dedicated databases, priority support, and higher SLAs. GTM is product-led growth with no-credit-card self-serve signup layered with enterprise direct sales via cal.com/talk-to-sales. Distribution extends to iOS, Android, Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox, macOS, Windows, and Linux apps and an affiliate/partner channel. Notable deployments include Deel (1,200+ users), Vercel, Supabase, Navi (HIPAA-regulated), Mintlify, and Kent C. Dodds / EpicWeb.dev. The platform reports over 1 million users, 4+ million bookings processed, and 150k+ calendar authorizations.

Cal.com is privately held and has raised $32.4 million in disclosed venture funding — a $7.4M seed led by OSS Capital in December 2021 and a $25M Series A led by Seven Seven Six in April 2022 — to expand its open-source scheduling infrastructure and build the 'App Store for Time' developer ecosystem. Leadership comprises co-founder/CEO Bailey Pumfleet and co-founder/Chairman Peer Richelsen (also serving as the company's EU GDPR representative). In March 2026 the company released Cal.com Agents (v6.3) extending Cal.ai into conversational scheduling across Slack, Telegram, email, CLI, and voice, and in April 2026 it transitioned the production codebase from AGPL-3.0 to closed source — citing AI-powered security threats — while launching Cal.diy, an MIT-licensed open-source community version, to retain hobbyists and self-hosting users.

recent_move.description: Transitioned the production codebase from AGPL-3.0 open source to closed source, citing AI-powered security threats against transparent open code as the justification.
Launched Cal.diy, an MIT-licensed open-source self-hostable version of the platform, to retain hobbyists and developers after the closed-source pivot.
Released Cal.com Agents (v6.3) extending Cal.ai into conversational scheduling across Slack, Telegram, email, CLI, and voice channels, alongside new OAuth scopes and custom-domain/SMTP controls.
Closed a $25 million Series A led by Seven Seven Six to expand scheduling infrastructure and launch the 'App Store for Time' developer ecosystem.
Raised a $7.4 million seed round led by OSS Capital to build extensible open-source scheduling infrastructure.

expansion_highlight.description: HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, and ISO 27001 certifications plus dedicated healthcare and telehealth landing pages signal a deliberate push into regulated clinical workflows. Navi is already deployed in this segment.

Cal.ai (voice + conversational agents) and the March 2026 Cal.com Agents release extend the platform beyond scheduling UI into AI-mediated meeting coordination, opening an agentic AI TAM adjacent to calendaring.

65+ language support, GDPR and CCPA compliance, and an appointed EU Representative indicate infrastructure built for international rollout, with North America the prioritized region (45.96% regional market share).

The 'App Store for Time' initiative (announced April 2022) plus the public REST API v2, OAuth scopes, Cal Atoms embeddables, and webhooks collectively pursue a developer-platform strategy that compounds distribution beyond direct sales.

Addition of multi-year enterprise contracts, dedicated databases, and priority support indicates a maturing upmarket GTM motion layered on top of the freemium PLG base, suggesting pricing-tier differentiation efforts to capture larger ACVs.
